systems.title: Power
systems.description: Follow energy from the source to the rack. Required foundations now; specialist power depth later, with electrical ownership kept explicit.

components.title: Utility & switchgear
components.role: Receives incoming power and divides it into protected distribution paths.
components.input: Utility supply, switch positions and the approved electrical configuration.
components.output: Power on identified buses and branches, plus electrical status and measurements.
components.dependency: Transformers, protective devices and every series element must support the required normal and failure-state load.
components.failure: A lost source or shared upstream device can remove several apparently separate downstream feeds.

check.question: Do two rack feeds prove independent power?
check.answer: No. Trace both feeds upstream. A shared bus, switchboard or source can defeat the claimed independence; evaluate the specific failure the service must survive.

components.title: Generator & transfer switch
components.role: Supplies longer-duration energy and transfers permitted loads to an acceptable source.
components.input: Source-loss detection, start energy, fuel and transfer permissives.
components.output: An accepted alternate supply after the start, stabilization and transfer sequence.
components.dependency: The UPS must bridge the actual sequence; fuel, starting systems and load-step capability must remain available.
components.failure: A generator may start yet fail to accept load, allowing stored energy to expire before service is supported.

check.question: Why is a successful engine start insufficient?
check.answer: The service also needs acceptable voltage and frequency, permitted transfer and load acceptance. Timing and dependent systems determine whether the required service survives.

components.title: UPS & battery
components.role: Conditions power and provides bounded ride-through in supported operating modes.
components.input: Normal or bypass AC supply and usable stored energy.
components.output: A load supply whose protection depends on mode, rating and battery condition.
components.dependency: Inverter capacity, bypass availability, battery runtime and recharge must match the load and transition requirements.
components.failure: Bypass can leave equipment powered with reduced protection; exhausted or degraded batteries shorten ride-through.

check.question: Does a powered rack mean the UPS still provides battery protection?
check.answer: No. Identify the path carrying the load. Maintenance bypass can remove the UPS and its stored-energy support from that path, even while the service remains powered.

components.title: Rack PDU & server feeds
components.role: Distributes branch power to named server inlets; some units also meter or switch outlets.
components.input: Upstream A/B feeds and the actual equipment demand.
components.output: Power through individual outlets, connectors and server power supplies.
components.dependency: Outlet, phase, connector and surviving-feed limits must hold when one path is unavailable.
components.failure: A local current limit can be exceeded despite acceptable rack-average kW; shared upstream supply defeats cord diversity.

check.question: Why assess the surviving feed instead of only the normal load?
check.answer: A dual-supply server may shift most or all demand to one path. That remaining outlet, branch and supply must support the required load under the stated conditions.

systems.title: Cooling
systems.description: Trace heat from the rack to its final sink. Required foundations now; specialist cooling depth later, with mechanical ownership kept explicit.

components.title: Air handler & containment
components.role: Moves air through equipment and a heat exchanger while limiting supply/exhaust mixing.
components.input: Warm return air, an available cooling source and fan/control demand.
components.output: Air delivered to equipment inlets within the required operating envelope.
components.dependency: Fan performance, path resistance, sealing and upstream heat removal jointly determine useful cooling.
components.failure: Recirculation or bypass can create hot inlets even when room-level capacity appears sufficient.

check.question: Can a cool room average rule out a hot rack?
check.answer: No. Equipment depends on its inlet conditions. Exhaust recirculation or a restricted local path can overheat one rack while the average room reading stays acceptable.

components.title: Heat rejection plant
components.role: Transfers collected facility heat to the outdoor environment through the selected plant arrangement.
components.input: Returning heat, electrical energy and any required water supply.
components.output: A usable cooling source and rejected heat at the final sink.
components.dependency: Ambient conditions, heat-exchanger approach and resource availability bound the usable capacity.
components.failure: Upstream heat removal can fail while room units and CDU pumps remain running.

check.question: Does lower cooling energy always demonstrate improvement?
check.answer: No. Compare similar workload and ambient conditions while preserving the required temperatures, capacity and resilience. A smaller workload or lost cooling function can also reduce energy use.

components.title: Coolant distribution unit
components.role: Couples technology and facility cooling loops while maintaining their defined fluid and control interfaces.
components.input: IT heat, a usable facility-water interface and validated local measurements.
components.output: Heat transferred out of the technology loop plus flow, temperature and alarm evidence.
components.dependency: The final heat sink, exchanger approach, supported fluid conditions and residual air cooling remain necessary.
components.failure: Healthy communications and circulating pumps can coexist with insufficient heat transfer.

check.question: Why does CDU network reachability not prove cooling?
check.answer: Reachability establishes a communication path. Useful cooling also requires valid flow and temperature evidence, a functioning exchanger and an available facility-side heat sink.

components.title: Pump & control valve
components.role: Regulates fluid movement as part of an approved cooling sequence.
components.input: Start or position commands, permissives and measured process conditions.
components.output: Actuator feedback and a measurable contribution to flow, pressure or temperature.
components.dependency: Valid sensing, open flow paths, equipment eligibility and mechanical limits govern operation.
components.failure: A run indication or reached valve position may provide no useful cooling when the path or source is unavailable.

check.question: Does a pump-running bit prove useful flow?
check.answer: No. It reports one equipment state. Check valid flow or pressure evidence and the required sequence before concluding that the pump contributes to the cooling service.

systems.title: Network
systems.description: Priority now: D4 network engineering. Inspect packet paths, tenant boundaries, storage fabrics and management access.

components.title: Leaf–spine fabric
components.role: Carries endpoint traffic through a routed underlay and, where used, a VXLAN overlay.
components.input: Endpoint frames, routing state and VTEP reachability.
components.output: Forwarded traffic on the selected physical path with the required encapsulation.
components.dependency: Routes, adjacency resolution, hardware programming and supported MTU must agree on every relevant path.
components.failure: A healthy routing session can hide a broken next hop or MTU defect that drops selected traffic.

check.question: Why can small pings work while an application fails?
check.answer: The application may use larger packets or another ECMP path. Encapsulation adds overhead, so test required packet sizes and all relevant forwarding paths instead of relying on session state.

components.title: Tenant gateway & policy
components.role: Routes traffic within the intended tenant context and applies the required communication boundaries.
components.input: Tenant packets, endpoint identity, route membership and policy.
components.output: Permitted routed flows while preserving the intended tenant separation.
components.dependency: VRF, bridge-domain, VNI and route-import relationships must align with the approved design.
components.failure: Wrong route import or classification can isolate an allowed service or expose another tenant.

check.question: Does a unique route distinguisher authorize tenant connectivity?
check.answer: No. It makes otherwise identical routes distinct. Route-target membership and the surrounding routing and policy configuration determine where those routes are imported and usable.

components.title: Storage fabric
components.role: Connects authorized initiators to storage targets with controlled identity and transport behavior.
components.input: Host I/O, initiator identities, fabric login and active access policy.
components.output: Storage requests and responses delivered through the intended fabric paths.
components.dependency: Active zoning, array masking, target readiness and adequate credit return serve different roles.
components.failure: Incorrect authorization can hide a LUN; a slow-draining endpoint can spread congestion to unrelated traffic.

check.question: Does Fibre Channel zoning determine which LUN a host can use?
check.answer: Zoning permits communication with target ports. Array masking separately exposes the intended logical storage objects; both controls and their effective state must be checked.

components.title: Out-of-band management
components.role: Provides controlled administrative and recovery access separate from ordinary workload traffic.
components.input: Approved administrator sessions, management identity and service reachability.
components.output: Authorized console, inventory, diagnostic or recovery operations with accounting.
components.dependency: Management power, network and identity paths must survive the failure the design claims to cover.
components.failure: Shared dependencies can remove recovery access with production; excessive management authority can affect many devices.

check.question: When is an out-of-band path actually independent?
check.answer: When it avoids the relevant failed dependencies, including power, network and identity services. A dedicated-looking management port alone does not establish that independence.

systems.title: Compute
systems.description: Mandatory now: D5 hardware and supporting platforms. Connect component behavior to workload performance, integrity and recovery.

components.title: CPU & memory
components.role: Executes instructions and supplies the working data through caches and memory channels.
components.input: Instructions, data, supported memory population and operating power/cooling.
components.output: Workload results with measurable latency, throughput and memory-error evidence.
components.dependency: Memory bandwidth, NUMA placement, firmware and thermal conditions can limit the service before core count does.
components.failure: Remote memory, channel imbalance or hardware/thermal faults can degrade service despite apparently spare CPU.

check.question: Can low CPU utilization rule out a compute bottleneck?
check.answer: No. A workload may wait on memory latency, bandwidth or another dependency. Use representative workload evidence and discriminating checks before treating the processor as the cause.

components.title: GPU & PCIe paths
components.role: Accelerates suitable parallel work while exchanging data with host memory, peers and network adapters.
components.input: Prepared workload data, driver/runtime state and accelerator commands.
components.output: Computed results and workload-specific completion or performance evidence.
components.dependency: Device memory, PCIe locality, supported firmware and fabric behavior constrain useful throughput.
components.failure: Data starvation, topology mismatches or RDMA errors can stall a distributed job without a failed GPU.

check.question: Does high GPU utilization prove a useful performance result?
check.answer: No. Measure the application outcome under stated conditions. Data movement, communication waits or unsuitable kernels can consume resources without meeting the required throughput or latency.

components.title: Storage array & host paths
components.role: Persists data and exposes it through identified storage objects and coordinated access paths.
components.input: Read/write requests, stable storage identities and host path policy.
components.output: Durable data service with measured latency, integrity and recovery behavior.
components.dependency: Media resilience, controller state, fabric access and host multipathing cover distinct failures.
components.failure: A common target dependency or incorrect recovery can interrupt I/O even when the host lists multiple paths.

check.question: Do two visible storage paths prove full redundancy?
check.answer: No. They can share an adapter, switch, controller or array. Trace shared points and test the stated path failure while checking application I/O and data integrity.

components.title: Hypervisor & virtual switch
components.role: Hosts workloads and maps their virtual interfaces onto supported physical resources and policies.
components.input: Guest traffic, virtual-network configuration and the approved host baseline.
components.output: Workload execution and packet forwarding through the actual virtual or passthrough path.
components.dependency: Virtualization manager, port group, encapsulation, uplinks and physical fabric attachments must agree.
components.failure: A visible VM can remain disconnected; passthrough can change enforcement, capture and migration behavior.

check.question: Does discovering a VM prove its network policy is deployed?
check.answer: No. Inventory and forwarding are separate states. Verify the virtual switch or passthrough path, encapsulation, uplink and physical attachment using the required application flow.

systems.title: Controls
systems.description: Priority now: D6 controls engineering. Follow the measurement, decision and command chain across physical equipment and supervisory software.

components.title: Sensor & field I/O
components.role: Turns a physical quantity at a known location into a qualified engineering observation.
components.input: The measurand, transmitter signal, wiring and configured measurement range.
components.output: A value with units, identity, time and quality for controller and operator decisions.
components.dependency: Placement, calibration, wiring, conversion and point mapping must preserve the same physical meaning.
components.failure: A plausible but frozen or wrongly scaled value can mislead both control logic and cybersecurity analysis.

check.question: Can an authenticated sensor still give misleading data?
check.answer: Yes. Authentication identifies a source; it does not prove calibration, placement, freshness or mapping. Validate the physical-to-logical chain and retain bad or uncertain quality states.

components.title: PLC & sequence logic
components.role: Evaluates process inputs and executes stateful control within the selected controller timing model.
components.input: Sampled inputs, valid permissives, operating mode and approved logic.
components.output: Commands, sequence state, diagnostics and bounded fault transitions.
components.dependency: Task scheduling, I/O updates, feedback deadlines and equipment eligibility must match the control narrative.
components.failure: Missed pulses, stale permissives or ambiguous state transitions can cause incorrect equipment behavior.

check.question: Why is an issued start command not proof of a successful start?
check.answer: A command records intent. The sequence needs timely equipment feedback and the required process contribution; otherwise it must follow the specified fault or fallback transition.

components.title: BMS, EPMS & historian
components.role: Presents mechanical/electrical state, alarms and historical evidence to operators.
components.input: Field observations, source quality/time, status feedback and approved supervisory commands.
components.output: Qualified displays, alarm transitions, event history and operational decision support.
components.dependency: Point identity, timestamps, collection health, alarm meaning and clear control ownership must survive integration.
components.failure: Fresh-looking displays can repeat stale data or present a request bit as proof of physical equipment state.

check.question: Does a green breaker-close request prove the breaker closed?
check.answer: No. A request expresses intent. Use the defined physical feedback and qualified observations; supervisory integration must preserve the distinction between command, status and actual function.

components.title: Protocol & serial gateway
components.role: Connects supported field and IP interfaces while preserving device identity and point semantics.
components.input: Serial frames or IP requests, device addressing and the verified register map.
components.output: Translated observations or authorized operations with interpretable transaction evidence.
components.dependency: Electrical bus design, framing/timing, unit addressing and scale/order conventions must align.
components.failure: A plausible value can belong to the wrong point; a write request may be observed without being accepted or applied.

check.question: Does seeing a Modbus write request prove the process changed?
check.answer: No. Reconstruct the request and response in connection and unit context, then examine controller state and physical outcome. Network intent, acceptance and process effect are distinct evidence.

systems.title: Security
systems.description: Priority now: D7 cybersecurity. Protect authorized operations, preserve evidence and restore trust across the connected data center.

components.title: Zone firewall
components.role: Enforces approved communication between zones with explicit routing, policy and connection-state behavior.
components.input: Packets, flow requirements and the current approved security policy.
components.output: Permitted or denied flows with usable enforcement and event evidence.
components.dependency: Actual routes, alternate paths, connection state and management authority must support the intended boundary.
components.failure: A rule change can block new sessions while leaving existing authority active; failover can expose a different path.

check.question: Does deleting an allow rule immediately revoke every session?
check.answer: Not necessarily. Established connection state can preserve access. Define the required revocation behavior and verify both new and existing sessions on the actual enforcement paths.

components.title: Remote access broker
components.role: Constrains maintenance access to an accountable person, approved target, task and session.
components.input: Verified identity, work authorization, target scope and permitted time window.
components.output: A bounded engineering session with target-level authority and audit linkage.
components.dependency: Broker identity, downstream accounts, API paths and session expiry must enforce the same approved scope.
components.failure: A valid login or recorded desktop session can coexist with excessive target permissions or an unobserved API path.

check.question: Does MFA make a remote engineering session authorized for every action?
check.answer: No. MFA strengthens authentication. The approved task, target operations, downstream credentials and session lifecycle determine what the engineer may actually do.

components.title: Identity & certificate services
components.role: Binds people and services to authenticated identities, current roles and intended peers.
components.input: Identity proof, authenticators, trust anchors and approved authorization policy.
components.output: Verified sessions and service relationships with scoped authority.
components.dependency: Time, certificate purpose, trust distribution, renewal and recovery must remain consistent across consumers.
components.failure: Restoring an old snapshot can revive departed users, obsolete trust anchors or temporary administrator rights.

check.question: Should a restored identity backup be accepted exactly as saved?
check.answer: No. Reconcile it with current authorized roles and trusted peers. Historical validity does not establish present authority, and required new identities may also be missing.

components.title: Monitoring sensor & evidence
components.role: Collects network and system observations that support defensible detection and incident analysis.
components.input: TAP/mirror traffic, endpoint events, controller changes and qualified process observations.
components.output: Correlated evidence and tested detection hypotheses with explicit coverage limits.
components.dependency: Collection capacity, placement, source identity, clock quality and capture health determine what is observable.
components.failure: Dropped traffic or missing paths can create false confidence; matching timestamps alone can imply a false causal story.

check.question: Does no alert prove there was no unauthorized control action?
check.answer: No. First establish visibility and collection health. Correlate request, acceptance, controller change and process outcome, and retain competing explanations where evidence is incomplete.
